merged_body: File-size split convention for native/angr/src (established angr-a2br.2 context.rs split, angr-7hwz value.rs split; test-file ambiguity resolved by angr-5mnx3.49 commit 5a84a60a0): every file — PROD AND TEST ALIKE — stays under ~2000 lines. Test files are NOT exempt; angr-p3bi's close text mused the owner 'may rule test files exempt' but the repo's actual shape had already settled the other way (vex/ops/tests_vec_*.rs, symbolic/value_ops_property_tests.rs, symbolic/value_z3_fp_tests.rs are all one-topic-per-file siblings). The split recipe, in order: (1) cut along the section banners already in the file — they are the author's own topic boundaries and land on test boundaries; (2) give each new file a //! module doc naming its scope and cross-referencing its siblings; (3) register each with test_submod!(z3 "file.rs" => modname) from the PROD file (keeping the same z3 gate — see no-default-features-test-gating), NOT from mod.rs; (4) a helper used by MORE THAN ONE resulting module moves to a shared <base>_tests_support.rs as pub(super) — sibling test modules are all children of the same prod module, so super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves; a helper used by exactly one stays private there. VERIFY the split lost nothing: grep -c the fn decls before and after (must match) and confirm cargo test --release reports the SAME pass count, not merely green. Then rename-sweep: moving a test between modules breaks doc citations of the form `module::test_name` — the value_tests split had 2 in-repo (value_ops_property_tests.rs) plus 7 bd memories to repair. PROD-side addendum (angr-5mnx3.1, arch/mod.rs -> register_file.rs + registry.rs): moving an `impl` block out of a mod.rs into a sibling breaks two things the type-checker only reports one at a time. (1) A method that was PRIVATE in the impl was visible to the `mod_tests.rs` sibling (both descendants of the same module); once the impl lives one level deeper it is not — widen exactly those to pub(super), not the whole impl. (2) An item that was DEFINED in mod.rs and is read only by tests (ArchDesc/ALL_ARCHES) becomes an `unused_imports` warning the moment it is re-exported instead, because the plain lib build has no consumer — CI clippy is --all-targets -D warnings, so it reds. Fix by making the sibling `pub(crate) mod` and having the tests path through it, keeping the re-export for the members lib code actually uses. (3) A type the moved code references ONLY in an intra-doc link (`[`SymContext`]` in a doc comment) must still be imported for rustdoc to resolve it, but rustc's unused_imports pass does NOT count doc-link uses — so the import warns and CI clippy -D warnings reds. Spell it `#[expect(unused_imports, reason = "referenced only by the intra-doc links below")]` rather than `allow`: if a later edit gives the import a real code use, unfulfilled_lint_expectations tells you to drop the attribute, whereas an `allow` would sit there forever. Seen in angr-fs8kb.35 (context.rs -> context_snapshot.rs / local_constraints.rs, both of which only name SymContext in prose). (4) angr-fs8kb.44 (sprintf.rs -> sprintf_spec.rs/sprintf_conv.rs, scanf.rs -> scanf_spec.rs): the `_tests.rs` sibling reaches the prod file's private items through `use super::*`, so ANY const/helper you move out of the prod file into a new sibling module breaks the test file even when the move is pure code motion and nothing changed visibility. rustc reports it as E0425 'cannot find value X in this scope' in the TEST file, pointing at the moved definition -- which reads like a visibility bug and is not; the fix is an explicit `use crate::<path>::<new_mod>::{X, y};` in the test file, plus pub(super) on the moved item. Corollary: do NOT keep the moved item imported in the prod file just to re-expose it to `super::*` -- with no lib-side consumer that is an unused_imports warning and CI clippy -D warnings reds, same trap as (2) above. (5) angr-fs8kb.20 (opcode_map.rs -> opcode_map_float.rs/opcode_map_vector.rs): when the prod file defines `macro_rules!` that the moved code invokes, textual macro scope does NOT follow the code to a SIBLING module (it covers only the defining module and its children), so each macro needs a `pub(super) use <name>;` line immediately after its definition and the new module imports it by path. Second half of the same trap: macro bodies name types unqualified (IROp/IRType/FCmpKind here) and macro_rules paths resolve at the CALL site, so the correct import list for each new module is whatever ITS OWN invocations expand to -- not a copy of the parent's `use` line. Expect the parent to shed an import as a result (FCmpKind became unused in opcode_map.rs once the fcmp_* invocations left), which CI clippy -D warnings will red. Verification for a macro-heavy split: grep -c the macro invocations (`_arms!`) as well as the fn decls before and after. (6) angr-fs8kb.66 (expressions.rs -> expressions_loads.rs/expressions_arith.rs): a baseline-gated audit script (tools/audit_silent_fallback.py and its four siblings) keys each known site by RELATIVE PATH, so moving a baselined line into a new file makes the gate report it as a NEW untagged site -- with the old entry now orphaned and silently unenforced. Fix by editing the one path in the baseline .txt (keeping its sorted position), NOT by --update-baseline, which would re-accept every other drift in the same run. Same reasoning as the pinned-baseline rule in run_regression.py: a refresh command hides the diff a hand edit makes reviewable. (7) angr-fs8kb.96 (statements_tests.rs -> statements_dirty_tests.rs/statements_cas_tests.rs): rule (4)'s `super::<base>_tests_support::helper resolves` claim holds ONLY while every test module is registered from the SAME prod file. When the split is PER PROD SIBLING -- each test module registered from the file it covers, which is the shape rule (3) pushes you toward once the prod side is already split -- the consumers are children of DIFFERENT prod modules and no `super::` path reaches across them. Register the support module one level up, from the package's mod.rs, and have each test module import it by full crate path (`use crate::interpreter::statements_tests_support::{..};`). `pub(super)` on the helpers is still the right visibility: super is now the package module, so it scopes them to exactly the subtree that may use them, without widening to pub(crate). This is the one sanctioned exception to rule (3)'s register-from-the-prod-file-not-mod.rs -- and it applies to the SUPPORT module only; the test modules themselves still register from their own prod sibling. (8) [absorbed from invariant-file-move-rebaselines-citations] The same path-keying bites tools/check_line_citations.py: its baseline rows are <path>\t<comment-text>, so a file split/move re-reds the gate with the baselined line citation reappearing as NEW under the new path. Preferred fix is to SYMBOL-ANCHOR the moved citation (per CLAUDE.md's symbol-anchor convention) and DELETE the old baseline row -- shrinking the debt rather than relocating it; repath the row only when the target has no resolvable symbol; never --update-baseline (seen angr-c7xno.45, expressions.rs -> expressions_inspect.rs). (9) [absorbed from invariant-module-split-test-file-boundaries] When splitting a prod module, split its sibling <mod>_tests.rs along the SAME boundaries. Section-banner markers are a starting point, not a trustworthy cut line: in helpers_tests.rs (angr-9ke6b.76) one '// --- Timeout / LengthLimiter / LoopBound ---' banner covered ~460 lines that also held the effective_pc tests and the materialize_deferred_forks block, and slicing on banners left dangling doc comments ('error: expected item after doc comment') plus cross-file fixture refs. Reliable method: list every top-level fn with line numbers and classify by the symbol it exercises, not the banner above it; walk BACKWARD from each fn over contiguous ///, // and #[..] lines to find the true block start; after cutting, grep each new file's head/tail for a trailing doc comment or orphaned fixture. A shared fixture with a single remaining consumer (e.g. push_active_at) moves with that consumer or is inlined; multi-consumer ones go to the support module per (4)/(7). Never hand-write the old '#[cfg(test)] #[path=..] #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used..)] mod x;' block -- every site goes through lib.rs's crate-root test_submod! (arms: test_submod!("f.rs" => name), test_submod!(name), optional 'z3 ' prefix for the cfg(all(test, feature="vex-engine-z3")) gate; invoke unqualified, #[path] resolves relative to the invoking file). DOC DUPLICATION (angr-5mnx3.69): extraction leaves two copies of a submodule's op-set description -- the doc comment on 'mod X;' in the parent and the file's own //! header -- and later op moves update only the header (vex/ops/mod.rs had three stale decl comments). When moving an op between submodules, fix the parent's 'mod <target>;' decl comment in the SAME commit; prefer keeping decl comments to placement/visibility rationale and letting the //! header own the inventory.

merged_body: After Phase 1.1, an address byte in Rust SymbolicMemory can be in one of four states: (1) pure Concrete (no bitmap bits, no sidecar entries); (2) plain Symbolic (page.is_symbolic bit set, entry in symbolic_objects and/or symbolic_spans, NOT in multi_objects); (3) Multi (page.is_multi bit set, entry in multi_objects, NOT in symbolic_objects — set_multi_alternatives clears the symbolic entries); (4) inconsistent/transitional (any other combination, treated as a bug). The 'Multi supersedes Symbolic' rule is enforced by the set_multi_alternatives setter — see test_multi_supersedes_existing_symbolic in native/angr/src/memory/tests/multi/payload.rs. When transitioning a byte's state, clear the old sidecar entries before installing the new one. BOTH directions have a setter that does this and both MUST be used: Symbolic->Multi is `set_multi_alternatives`, Multi->Symbolic is `clear_multi_at` (drops the multi_objects payload AND the page multi_bitmap bit; safe no-op on a non-Multi byte). Note `MemoryPage::mark_symbolic` alone is NOT enough — it only touches symbolic_bitmap, so a path that marks a byte symbolic without `clear_multi_at` leaves state (4). This exact omission has now been found and fixed at every known Multi->Symbolic transition site, so treat any NEW one as guilty until it calls clear_multi_at: `SymbolicMemory::merge`'s collapse-a-Multi-side-into-an-ITE path (angr-0jh0j.31), `store_concrete`'s symbolic branch (angr-9ke6b.95), and `import_symbolic_value` (angr-6cp06.62 — the live flush_stores / flush_stores_to_rust_memory path, so it silently dropped ordinary symbolic stores at concretized addresses). The failure mode is identical in all three: load_concrete_common's range_has_multi check dispatches Multi-marked bytes to the Multi path BEFORE consulting symbolic_objects, and flush_multi_cells then writes the stale payload back over the new value on export. See also [[invariant-symbolic-byte-lane-lookup]] and [[invariant-every-load-path-gates-multi]]. CORRECTION + DISPATCH ORDER [absorbed from invariant-multi-symbolic-bitmap-dispatch-order]: state (3)'s 'NOT symbolic' holds for the SIDECAR only. set_multi_alternatives (memory/multi.rs) retires the symbolic_objects entry via retire_symbolic_object_at but never calls MemoryPage::clear_symbolic, so a byte promoted Symbolic->Multi keeps BOTH page bitmap bits set -- the symbolic_bitmap and multi_bitmap are NOT mutually exclusive and no code may assume they are. Multi wins by DISPATCH ORDER: every reader must probe Multi before Symbolic (load_concrete_common's range_has_multi gate, assemble_load_with_multi, compute_wider_load_fingerprint, merge::merge_byte_value's is_multi arm all do); a new reader that checks is_symbolic first silently resolves a Multi byte to a retired/absent symbolic object. Readers that want only CONCRETE bytes must check both bits, because install_multi_for_candidates on a never-symbolic byte sets only the multi bit -- read_concrete_bytes_for_lift missing this let the lifter decode MultiPayload::collapse's don't-care concrete_byte as an instruction byte (angr-4r8mh). The reverse transition is deliberately asymmetric: a symbolic store over a Multi cell DOES clear the multi bit (store_concrete -> clear_multi_at), since there a stale bit would win dispatch and shadow the fresh value. Pinned by collapse.rs::test_symbolic_overwrite_clears_multi_cell and test_lift_read_stops_at_multi_byte.

merged_body: Assert-hardening rule of thumb for a broken internal precondition (established in the automaton/epsilon_nfa.rs hardening, angr-9ke6b.191/.193), three tiers: (1) return a Result when the function is PyO3-reachable AND has few callers -- a Rust panic surfaces in Python as an opaque PanicException instead of a ValueError (EpsilonNFA::move_on_symbol now returns Result<StateSet, EpsilonSymbolError>, rippled through subset_construction to PyEpsilonNFA::minimize's PyValueError); (2) debug_assert! for a pure-internal worklist invariant whose violation would only mis-step (dfa.rs, angr-9ke6b.182); (3) unconditional panic! when skipping the bad input would produce a SILENTLY WRONG result in release builds -- EpsilonNFA::epsilon_closure panics on a stale-cache/out-of-range state id, because a dropped state means a wrong closure means a wrong DFA, and debug_assert! alone leaves release silently wrong. Both functions' rustdoc carries the per-site rationale. Complements debug-assert-triage-policy (which adds the fourth shape: when the enclosing fn already has an error channel, log and return that error in every profile).
